matches.rationale: Finding 2 challenges the exact numerical value of 14.6% as unverifiable, but the ground truth is about missing confidence intervals and overclaimed universality, not a fabrication of the number. Different scientific issues.
Finding 1 identifies a Menon & Vondrick year inconsistency, not the fabricated 1892 Filippini reference. Different citation error.
No finding describes the inconsistency between how action embeddings are computed (difference) and how they are used in loss/prediction heads.
No finding mentions missing hyperparameter tuning details for baselines. Finding 7 notes suspiciously identical scores but not the methodological omission.
No finding points out the absence of variance or confidence intervals for precision scores in Table 1.
No finding addresses the lack of ethical, bias, or responsible AI discussion in the conclusion.
No finding mentions the contradiction between ground-truth labels in Sec 3.1 and pseudo-labeled/noisy estimates in Sec 3.2.
No finding flags the inflated rhetorical language ('powerful', 'promising pathway') in the introduction.
No finding discusses the suspiciously similar precision in Table 4 despite tripling the number of graph concepts.
No finding addresses the ambiguous role of privileged information (object/action labels) during evaluation.
No finding mentions the disproportionate training times (8 h vs 30 min) for similarly sized datasets.
No finding points out the missing criteria or thresholds for VLM-based frame filtering in Sec 3.1.
No finding identifies the mismatch between claimed multi-action generalization and the use of only single-action evaluation datasets.
No finding addresses the exaggerated future-work claims in the conclusion that imply already-solved perception challenges.
No finding discusses the unexplained sharp baseline degradation on novel objects in Table 2(b) or the lack of discussion around it.
